program: Housing, public-benefits legal aid and systemic advocacy

what: Inner City Law Center combines eviction defense with benefits access, housing-condition litigation and policy advocacy in Los Angeles.
Its legal services can protect housing and income for people facing serious disadvantage.
The numerical scenario below prices only the short-term health contribution of eviction prevention against recipient-wide costs; it is not a complete portfolio valuation.
strengths: A concrete route connects legal representation to housing stability, with some randomized evidence that representation changes possession outcomes.
The recipient reports completed cases and housing outcomes, not only consultations.
Public-benefits and systemic work may deliver important benefits beyond the priced housing component.
reservations: Reported evictions prevented are not a comparison with what would have happened without assistance.
Current public right-to-counsel funding and other legal-aid providers may replace part of a new gift.
Health utility, marginal funding response and donated-resource accounting remain judgmental or unreconciled.

sections.what: ICLC provides tenant defense, benefits assistance, housing-condition litigation and systemic advocacy. The [current program description](https://innercitylaw.org/what-we-do/) places these services within a broader anti-homelessness portfolio, not an eviction-only charity. Current clinics and 2026 activity establish continuing operations.
sections.monitoring: The [2024 impact report](https://innercitylaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/2024-ICLC-Impact-Report.pdf) records 875 evictions prevented, 1,589 cases closed and 3,403 people served. These categories overlap and are not added. It does not establish unique counterfactual evictions averted or sustained health effects. The most useful next evidence would link distinct cases to housing and health at six and twelve months, alongside a comparable untreated or differently served group.
sections.qualitative: The [District Court randomized trial](https://harvardlawreview.org/print/vol-126/the-limits-of-unbundled-legal-assistance-a-randomized-study-in-a-massachusetts-district-court-and-prospects-for-the-future/) found substantially better possession outcomes from full representation than limited assistance in a selected setting. The companion [Housing Court experiment](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/sites/default/files/research-paper/3826_Legal%20assistance%20programs%20Mar2012.pdf) found no significant advantage, supporting a genuine zero case. Separately, [judge-assignment research](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10772599/) connects eviction to subsequent housing instability and hospital use; it does not supply a QALY conversion. Benefits recovery, better housing conditions and policy work are important but unpriced here.
sections.cost:
The current conditional joint reference is $21459462.00 per ten LA healthy-year equivalents: 2.4975728155339807 clinical QALYs plus 12.767436622495753 signed resource-equivalent years at $32,757,889 reconstructed full annual recipient resources. The original health-only reference remains a diagnostic, not the current joint price. This is an illustrative source-linked judgment, not observed net cash, empirical calibration or complete portfolio value.

The [2024 impact report](https://innercitylaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/2024-ICLC-Impact-Report.pdf) records $20,545,491.27 recovered for clients; [programs](https://innercitylaw.org/what-we-do/) identify settlement awards and recovered benefits. We do not count all legal matters as wins or assume the 44% below $10,000 statistic is the whole-cohort disposable baseline. The reference uses 0.4 household-equivalents per 3,403 served people, distributing the recovery pool across 1,361.2 hypothetical resource-sharing households. Capacity0.5 creates680.6 responsive households; payment additionality0.25 gives170.15 positive-conversion households. Recovery conversion0.5, net retention0.8 and positive overlap0.5 are explicit judgments.

Each responsive household bears the full hypothetical $100 incremental access, administration and opportunity loss regardless of clinical or legal-payment success. This is not observed burden and excludes provider resources already in cost; overlap sensitivity removes it. Baseline $15,000 is a judgment, with wide sensitivity. Gains and costs are jointly logged at household level. Recovery is one-time, consumed over one year after one-year delay, not a repeated annual flow. Taxes, withdrawn benefits and replacement awards are in net retention. Landlord/public transfers and disjoint payer or real-resource costs have separate alternatives, without duplicate transfers. Existing counsel, public funding and enacted policies continue. No retail housing value, gross wages or ordinary survivor earnings is credited; broader portfolio and unrestricted-gift expectation remain unknown.

The original returns imply gross Form 990 accrual expenses of $17,090,749 in 2022, $18,745,042 in 2023 and $20,403,467 in 2024, including separately netted event costs. Their mean is $18,746,419. The central resource denominator adds the report’s $12,354,422 donated-service valuation to 2024 Form 990 expenses, reaching $32,757,889. This reconstruction exceeds the impact report’s total by $146,191 and is not a verified audit reconciliation. The conditional housing-health price is about $131.2 million per ten LA QALYs; sensitivity excluding donated legal services is $81.7 million. Neither number values the full portfolio, and neither supports ranking ICLC as though its other work had zero value.
sections.funding: A general gift can sustain staff, coordination and cases not completely financed by contracts. The [original 2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953697572/202513169349303841/full) reports positive annual net income and substantial net assets; those balances do not establish unrestricted cash available for every program. Current [public-funding advocacy](https://innercitylaw.org/) and already adopted tenant protections belong in the baseline. We assume only half of annual activity-equivalent funding translates into additional services after financing substitution, with zero retained as a plausible outcome. No verified immediate funding gap or extra-case commitment was found.

model.costScope: Recipient-wide annual cost, not tenant-defense program cost. The central reconstruction adds the separately reported donated legal-service valuation to 2024 gross accrual Form 990 expenses. It is not an audited full-resource amount: the $146,191 reconciliation gap remains. Sensitivities use Form 990 gross expense excluding donated legal services and the impact report's stated total. The numerator prices only short-term eviction-related health, not a whole-portfolio return or full societal analysis.
model.geographicAttribution: LA MSA is Los Angeles and Orange counties. Direct legal services are Los Angeles-focused; g=.98 is a judgment allowance for beneficiary residence outside the boundary, not an observed geocoded share. Statewide policy spillovers are unpriced.
model.formula: Q_all=N*d*a*b*q/(1+r); Q_LA=g*Q_all; price10=10*C/Q_LA. N=875 reported prevention outcomes; d=.8 unique relevant index clients; a=.25 genuinely incremental versus alternatives; b=.5 marginal funding response; q=.06 utility improvement for .5 year=.03 QALY; r=.03 one-year delay; g=.98; C=20,326,674+76,793+12,354,422=32,757,889. No household-size multiplier, recurring annual credit or separate hospital/benefits QALYs.
model.counterfactual: Existing public contracts, right-to-counsel programs, limited assistance, other counsel, tenant self-help and settlements continue. a concerns legal outcome additionality at case level; b separately concerns whether more unrestricted resources change volume rather than replace existing finance. Already enacted policy wins are not new-gift benefits.
model.attribution: No coalition policy credit is claimed. d reduces possible repeated or insufficiently defined prevention records. Only one index client receives the finite utility benefit; financial recovery and family members are not added.
model.uncertainty: Subjective conditional component model, not a causal estimate of ICLC or probability confidence interval. External trials justify a possible legal mechanism and a zero scenario, not these parameter values. Utility conversion is an explicit prior. Unpriced portfolio may dominate, so do not use this component price as a complete rank.
model.nativeOutcomes: 875 reported prevention outcomes become 700 distinct relevant cases, 175 incremental preventions and 87.5 funding-attributable preventions before geography; 85.75 within LA under the central assumptions. Six-month health improvement is hypothetical, not measured.

inputs.name: d

inputs.rationale: Deduplication and classification allowance; .6–1 scenarios, no empirical ICLC rate.

inputs.name: a
inputs.unit: incremental prevention fraction versus other assistance
inputs.rationale: Judgment informed by positive and null legal-aid trials; not their ITT coefficient or an ICLC causal rate.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: No current unrestricted marginal case schedule; range includes zero.

inputs.name: q
inputs.rationale: One index person improves utility by .06 for six months. Research supports health relevance, not this utility. No lifetime, mortality, household or earnings addition.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: LA beneficiary share for priced direct-service outcomes
inputs.rationale: Los Angeles service focus with residence allowance .9–1; no statewide policy allocation.

inputs.name: r
inputs.unit: annual discount rate; one-year delivery delay
inputs.rationale: Finite one-year timing adjustment; q already has six-month duration.

sensitivity: Central price is approximately $131.2m per ten LA QALYs, versus $81.7m on Form 990 gross expense; favorable component assumptions yield about $10.3m. Zero is not excluded.

For a whole-portfolio $1m per ten QALYs price, annual attributable LA health benefit must reach 327.57889 QALYs at reconstructed resource cost; at $100k it must reach 3275.7889. This is a diagnostic, not a claim that legal benefits are all health.
Halving funding responsiveness or utility doubles the conditional component price. Other portfolio outcomes are not assigned a convenient multiplier.
